notes: There is no public transport in Phuket: use a scooter (licence and helmet required), Grab or a hotel taxi. Tuk-tuks are expensive, so haggle.
June to October is monsoon season: don't swim when the red flag is up (currents), boat tours may be cancelled, and showers fall in the afternoon. Favour Phang Nga Bay and indoor activities.
Book boat tours online with hotel pickup included, and bring seasickness pills and reef-safe sunscreen.
Choose seafood by the kilo at Rawai market; the cooking fee is charged separately per person.
Cover shoulders and knees at temples; on Bangla Road, ask the price of drinks first.
Don't ride elephants; choose ethical sanctuaries.

stops.name: Phuket Old Town Thalang Road
stops.tips: Colourful Sino-Portuguese shopfronts; cafes open in the morning, and on Sundays the street becomes a pedestrian market.

stops.name: Phuket Thai Hua Museum
stops.tips: The story of Chinese immigrants, in an air-conditioned former school building.

stops.name: One Chun Cafe Phuket
stops.tips: Michelin Bib Gourmand local cooking; try moo hong (braised pork belly) and crab.

stops.name: Big Buddha Phuket
stops.tips: A 45 m marble Buddha on the hilltop with 360° views of the island. Cover shoulders and knees; get there by taxi or scooter.

stops.name: Wat Chalong
stops.tips: Phuket's most important temple, known for the firecracker wish-making tradition.

backups.name: Khao Rang Hill
backups.tips: A hilltop viewpoint over the city, close to Big Buddha, so a good alternative.

stops.name: Kata Noi Beach
stops.tips: Monsoon swells: don't swim when the red flag is up. Come in the morning for a walk or a surf lesson.

stops.name: Kata Beach Street Stalls
stops.tips: Pad thai and mango sticky rice just behind the beach.

stops.name: Karon Beach
stops.tips: An empty beach in summer, good for a walk and watching the waves.

stops.name: Karon Viewpoint
stops.tips: A viewpoint that takes in three bays at once; go before sunset.

stops.name: Kata Night Market
stops.tips: A night market in central Kata with grilled seafood and roti.

backups.name: Kampong Kata Hill Restaurant
backups.tips: A Thai restaurant packed with antiques, in Kata.

backups.name: Dino Park Mini Golf
backups.tips: A rainy-day option for families with kids, in Karon.

stops.name: James Bond Island Khao Phing Kan
stops.tips: Canoe tour (~1,500 THB). The bay stays calm even in summer, with limestone islands and caves.

stops.name: Koh Panyee
stops.tips: A Muslim fishing village built on stilts; have lunch on the boat.

stops.name: Hong Island Kano
stops.tips: Canoe into the sea caves; included in the tour.

stops.name: Suwan Kuha Temple
stops.tips: A cave temple with monkeys and a reclining Buddha.

stops.name: Rawai Seafood Market
stops.tips: Pick your fish at the market in Rawai and have it cooked across the way. Phuket's most famous seafood evening.

backups.name: Kan Eang at Pier Chalong
backups.tips: Seafood at Chalong Pier, as an alternative to Rawai.

backups.name: Coral Island Koh Hae
backups.tips: A nearby island for a half-day trip if Phi Phi is cancelled.

stops.name: Freedom Beach
stops.tips: Boats don't run in monsoon swells; instead, walk to Tri Trang beach from Patong.

stops.name: Patong Beach
stops.tips: The island's busiest beach: good for a walk and jet skis (haggle).

stops.name: No.6 Restaurant Patong
stops.tips: A cheap Thai eatery in Patong with a fast-moving queue; try the tom yum.

stops.name: Jungceylon Shopping Mall
stops.tips: An air-conditioned mall for a break from the rain and heat.

stops.name: Bangla Road
stops.tips: Patong's nightlife street with bars and shows; watch your wallet.

backups.name: Baan Rim Pa Patong
backups.tips: Royal Thai cuisine on the cliffs, with sunset views.

backups.name: Simon Cabaret Phuket
backups.tips: A cabaret show, as an alternative to Bangla Road.

stops.name: Nai Harn Beach
stops.tips: Monsoon swells. Come in the morning for a walk and a stroll along the lake.

stops.name: Nai Harn Beach Stalls
stops.tips: Grilled food and fruit shakes behind the beach.

stops.name: Windmill Viewpoint
stops.tips: A viewpoint by the wind turbine, looking over Nai Harn and Ya Nui.

stops.name: Promthep Cape
stops.tips: The island's southernmost tip and Phuket's most famous sunset; claim a spot an hour early.

backups.name: Rawai Beach Restaurant
backups.tips: Thai food on the Rawai seafront.

backups.name: Ya Nui Beach
backups.tips: A tiny snorkelling cove below Promthep.

stops.name: Phuket Elephant Sanctuary
stops.tips: An ethical elephant sanctuary: half a day of feeding and mud baths (~3,000 THB), with no riding.

stops.name: Elephant Sanctuary Vegetarian Lunch
stops.tips: Vegetarian lunch included in the tour.

stops.name: Bang Pae Waterfall
stops.tips: A waterfall in the Khao Phra Thaeo forest, full of water in summer; a 20-minute walk.

backups.name: Gibbon Rehabilitation Project
backups.tips: Gibbon conservation, next to the waterfall.

days.theme: Old Town morning and a gentle goodbye

stops.name: Old Town Soi Romanee
stops.tips: The most photogenic street, best in the morning light.

stops.name: Torry's Ice Cream Phuket
stops.tips: Local ice cream in Old Town; try the coconut.

stops.name: Blue Elephant Phuket
stops.tips: Royal Thai cuisine in a mansion for a farewell lunch; cooking classes are also available.

stops.name: Phuket Airport Road Sirinat
stops.tips: The airport is 45 minutes away; time to say goodbye.

backups.name: Ka Jok See Phuket
backups.tips: Thai food in an old house.

backups.name: Sirinat National Park Nai Yang
backups.tips: A beach next to the airport, good for watching planes.
